$comment: The one place PAB's colours, type and spacing are written down (E1).
Android used #5B21B6 and the website used Tailwind's default purple-700 (#7E22CE), so the
two apps were different shades of purple side by side. These are Android's values, because
they were chosen for PAB's lavender ('Bringing the Lavender Back to the Hills'), and the
Run `npm run tokens` to write the Tailwind theme from this file, and
`node tools/tokens/build.js --android <path to PAB_Volunteers>` to write Android's
colors.xml. Neither is edited by hand. Android keeps its own spacing and radius names,
which are already used across its layouts, and its own dark palette, which is a second
scheme chosen for dark surfaces rather than these colours inverted.

brand.$comment: PAB's lavender, dark to light. 900 is the header band, 700 the primary action.

neutral.$comment: Greys tinted towards the brand, rather than flat grey (K7). 500 is the lightest that passes 4.5:1 on white, so nothing lighter is used for text.

$comment: One colour per status, the same on both apps and in the staff list (W12).
Each pairs with its own surface, and each pair passes 4.5:1, because these are read as
text on a pill and, on the confirmation page, as the emergency numbers themselves.
#DC2626 on #FEE2E2 measured 3.95:1 and #059669 on #D1FAE5 about 3.1:1, so both are a
step darker than the Tailwind default they started as.

onBrand.$comment: Text on a brand surface. muted is white at 85%, which passes 4.5:1 on brand-500; the old #D8B4FE did not (F9).

type.$comment: Lora for headings, Source Sans 3 for body. Inter was the web's body face and is the most common sign of generic design; Source Sans 3 carries isiXhosa and Afrikaans diacritics properly (E3).

space.$comment: A 4px step, as both platforms use.

target.$comment: The smallest a tappable control may be: 44px on the web (WCAG 2.5.5) and 48dp on Android (F5).
